item.title: Angels' Reid Detmers aims to continue strong run vs. Twins
item.description: Los Angeles Angels left-hander Reid Detmers will try to continue a strong finish to his breakout season on Saturday night when he faces the Minnesota Twins in Anaheim, Calif.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Angels left-hander Reid Detmers will try to continue a strong finish to his breakout season on Saturday night when he faces the Minnesota Twins in Anaheim, Calif. Detmers (6-8, 3.36 ERA) has a majors-best 1.65 ERA in 11 starts since the All-Star break with 76 strikeouts and 11 walks in 65 1/3 innings. He needs one more strikeout to become the 12th pitcher in franchise history to record 200 strikeouts in a season, and the first since Shohei Ohtani in 2022. Detmers is 1-2 with a 5.40 ERA in seven career appearances (five starts) against Minnesota. He brings a streak of seven consecutive quality starts into the contest after helping pitch Los Angeles (59-95) to a 6-4 victory over the Seattle Mariners on Monday, allowing three runs on seven hits and a walk in six innings with eight strikeouts. Cal Raleigh belted a three-run homer to snap a streak of six consecutive starts that Detmers made pitching at least six innings while allowing one or fewer runs. "I just felt like I didn't have my best stuff tonight, but was able to get through six and only give up the home run to Cal, so I was very satisfied with that," Detmers said. "You're not always going to have your best stuff, so sometimes you have to give and take with what you've got." Right-hander Joe Ryan (6-10, 3.84) will make his third start for Minnesota (72-82) since coming off the 15-day injured list with a left glute strain. Ryan is 2-0 with a 3.10 ERA in five career starts against Los Angeles with 41 strikeouts in 29 innings. He didn't figure in the decision in a 5-3 win over the Angels on July 11 at Target Field when he gave up two runs on six hits in six innings with two walks and six strikeouts. Ryan is 0-5 in five starts since the All-Star break and comes in off a 9-2 loss to the Cleveland Guardians on Sunday, allowing four runs on seven hits in four innings with just one strikeout. Steven Kwan homered on the second pitch of the game and Jo Adell added a solo homer in the third for Cleveland. He departed after throwing 84 pitches, 51 for strikes. "I think 'battle' is probably the best way to put it," Ryan said. "Just kind of long at-bats, throwing the ball for the most part where we wanted to throw it. They were just kind of beating me to it there. It's frustrating when it's a day like that, and yeah, they've had a pretty good approach all year I would say." Los Angeles posted a 5-4 win in 10 innings on Thursday before Minnesota evened the four-game series with a 3-0 victory on Friday night. Walker Jenkins homered and had his second straight three-hit game for the Twins. The 21-year-old Jenkins, ranked Minnesota's top prospect by MLB.com, entered the series batting .089 (4-for-45) with 16 strikeouts but is 6-for-8 with two home runs and three RBIs in the first two games against the Angels. "I think jumping levels, it's always mental," Jenkins said of overcoming his slow big league start. "I think obviously guys are better but it's a mental adjustment. Bigger stadiums, more people, better arms, and I think I just had to settle in a little bit. I wouldn't say I have it figured out yet, but we're going to continue to stack good days and hopefully help the team win." --Field Level Media

item.title: Mariners strive for strong finish, brace for rematch vs. Rockies
item.description: The playoffs likely aren't in the immediate future for the Seattle Mariners, but that won't impact how they play their final eight games.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The playoffs likely aren't in the immediate future for the Seattle Mariners, but that won't impact how they play their final eight games. Seattle (72-82) recorded a 5-4 victory Friday in the opener of a three-game series against the Colorado Rockies in Denver. The Mariners will take on the Rockies again on Saturday night, sending right-hander Bryce Miller (4-9, 4.19 ERA) to the mound. Miller has faced Colorado once in his career, giving up three runs on five hits in 5 2/3 innings in Seattle last Sept. 23. He received a no-decision in the Mariners' 4-3 win that clinched a playoff berth for the team and sparked a postseason path that nearly stretched to the franchise's first World Series appearance. This season, Seattle manager Dan Wilson wants to finish strong after his team dropped two of three games vs. the Los Angeles Angels ahead of the series with the Rockies. "We've got to keep going, we've got to keep playing," Wilson said of his team, which remains mathematically alive in the playoff race. "Coming out of a tough series there in Anaheim, I thought the first game and the last game really approached it well. We've got to continue to take that mentality and continue to do the things that make us successful offensively in a ballpark like this (Coors Field). "You've got to really find ways to add on. You've got to really push, and this is a ballpark where strange things can happen." Colorado (56-98) is accustomed to strange things happening in its home park, and the team has a knack of making things interesting with late rallies. The Rockies erased a 3-0 deficit to claim a 4-3 lead on Friday but couldn't hold on. While the rallies have been exciting, Colorado is on the verge of a fourth straight 100-loss season. The Rockies have improved from their 119-loss campaign in 2025 and surpassed last year's win total (43) before August of this season. However, since sitting 45-67 on Aug. 2, Colorado is 11-31 and has struggled to get solid starting pitching. The rotation has not recorded a win in 21 games but could get a boost with the return of left-hander Jose Quintana, 37, as the starter on Saturday. The veteran, who signed a one-year deal in the offseason, is 2-3 with a 5.27 ERA in nine starts this year, but his last one came May 24 at Arizona. A left elbow sprain has sidelined him since then, but he had a goal of pitching again before the end of the season. "He's a 15-year vet that got hurt in May -- it would be easy for a guy like that, with all that time, to just shut it down and call it a day," Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer said. "But he set an example for all the young players." Quintana is 2-2 with a 3.58 ERA in 13 career appearances (nine starts) vs. the Mariners. --Field Level Media

item.title: Martin recovers from early setback to win Austrian sprint and retake championship lead
item.description: Aprilia's Jorge Martin made an extraordinary recovery from a chaotic opening-lap battle with championship rival Marc Marquez to win the Austrian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Aprilia's Jorge Martin made an extraordinary recovery from a chaotic opening-lap battle with championship rival Marc Marquez to win the Austrian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead. Martin, who had stormed to [USN:L4N45B027 TEXT:"pole position"] ahead of reigning MotoGP champion Marquez earlier on Saturday, beat the Ducati rider to claim his 20th sprint victory after KTM's Pedro Acosta crashed out while leading in the closing stages. The 28-year-old Martin, the 2024 MotoGP champion, now has 286 points in the standings, three ahead of Spanish compatriot Marquez, heading into Sunday's Grand Prix at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg. Martin's race appeared to unravel in the opening corners when he was forced on to the defensive by seven-time MotoGP champion Marquez, ran wide and dropped to eighth. Acosta capitalised to take command and built a lead of nearly three seconds, only to crash out with about three laps remaining at KTM's home circuit. Martin, meanwhile, carved his way back through the pack to secure a remarkable victory. "I enjoyed the race for sure," Martin said. "I was a bit lucky with Pedro because we thought that I would be second. We started well but then we were on the limit on the first lap, so I thought my chances were over. "But then, lap by lap, I didn't give up during the race. I was pushing till my maximum, trying to be super concentrated to come from the back and then win. The end was so good. "I am really happy for my team because they really deserve it. We are ready for tomorrow. I hope that we can continue at this pace." Marquez had seized the championship lead for the first time this season by winning last weekend's chaotic [USN:L1N455030 TEXT:"San Marino Grand Prix"] . The result had left him level on points with Martin but the 33-year-old moved to the top of the standings by virtue of having won more races this season. "Today the target was third place in the sprint and I tried not to lose a lot of points against Jorge because it's already in practice that Pedro and Jorge had a better pace," Marquez said. "Then I found the position where I sat just behind Jorge, and we were a bit lucky with Pedro's mistake. But happy and ready for tomorrow." Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, third in the championship standings, completed the podium. Trackhouse Aprilia's Ai Ogura finished fourth with Alex Marquez fifth.

item.title: Israeli strikes kill three people in Gaza, medics say
item.description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Saturday, health officials said.
item.dc:creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
item.content:encoded: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Saturday, health officials said. One strike near Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza killed Basir Al-Bursh, the son of Munir Al-Bursh, the territory's health ministry director-general, medics and family members said. The Israeli military said it had struck several militants on Saturday, including Basir Al-Bursh, without giving further information. Hamas, the Palestinian militant group that runs Gaza, did not immediately comment. Munir Al-Bursh lost a daughter in an Israeli airstrike in December 2023, according to family members and medics. He was wounded in that attack. In video obtained by Reuters, Al-Bursh was seen carrying his son's body, wrapped in a blanket, with other mourners as it was rushed to hospital by ambulance. "I was with him in the tent, and he said, Dad, they will target us, you and me together, I said that is fine, we will go to heaven together," said Al-Bursh in the video. "He went outside the tent and they struck him and he was martyred, may God have mercy on him," added Al-Bursh. At Al Shifa Hospital, Al-Bursh could barely stand as mourners arrived to pay their respects. Elsewhere, a strike killed a man in Shejaia, east of Gaza City, while another hit a vehicle in the Sheikh Radwan district of Gaza City, killing one person, the civil defence service and medics said, taking Saturday's death toll to at least three. The Israeli military said the Sheikh Radwan strike targeted a Hamas militant. The blast reduced the vehicle to a mangled wreck. Palestinian authorities say more than 73,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023. A US-brokered [USN:L8N4590HK TEXT:"ceasefire"] agreed last year calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory, but little progress has been made as negotiators have failed to agree terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. More than 1,300 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to the territory's health officials, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed.

item.title: Torrid Padres take on Marlins, hoping to keep pace in NL wild-card race
item.description: Friday night couldn't have gone any better for the San Diego Padres.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Friday night couldn't have gone any better for the San Diego Padres. Not only did they continue their scalding September with an 8-2 defeat of the visiting Miami Marlins, but losses by the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia enabled the Padres (85-69) to forge a three-way tie atop the National League wild-card standings. And their magic number to clinch a playoff spot was reduced to four when the New York Yankees defeated Arizona. San Diego will hope for similar results on Saturday when it looks to improve to 5-0 this season against Miami. The Padres are presently flying on a rocket ship to the postseason. They've won 11 of their last 12 games and have scored at least six runs in seven of their last eight. The idea of actually hosting a wild-card series is now taking on serious traction. While San Diego would lose any tiebreaker with the Phillies or Cubs, it is easily the hottest of the three clubs coming down the home stretch. "The only thing that we can worry about is playing each game the best we can and playing to our standard," said manager Craig Stammen. "That first playoff game, we would love for it to be in San Diego." The Padres are 47-29 in Petco Park, including a 22-5 mark dating back to July 10. The only home series they've lost since late June came at Pittsburgh's hands in late August. "We're in a good spot going into these last eight games," said first baseman Ty France, who belted his career-high 21st homer to cap a six-run fifth inning Friday night. "Hopefully, we can just keep things going." Casey Mize (6-9, 3.69 ERA) will try to string together consecutive wins for San Diego. He scattered eight hits over five innings Monday night in an 8-7 victory at Colorado, allowing two runs. He is 1-1 with a 2.31 ERA in two prior starts against Miami. Eury Perez (7-11, 3.99) looks to escape the roughest patch of his season, one that's seen him allow 19 earned runs in his last four starts, covering 16 2/3 innings. The best start in that stretch came Sunday in a 6-4 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers. Perez made it through five innings, allowing four hits and three runs with two walks and five strikeouts. Control has been an issue as he's doled out 12 walks in that span. He's 0-1 with a 3.75 ERA in two career outings against San Diego. The loss came on July 25, when he worked seven innings and yielded three runs in an eventual 7-2 defeat that was the 11th game in a 12-game losing streak that eventually took Miami (76-78) out of the running. With Miami out of the playoffs for a third straight season, it will use the remaining time to try to find answers for an inconsistent bullpen. Season-ending injuries to closer Pete Fairbanks and setup man Anthony Bender have made things harder. Manager Clayton McCullough said he won't have a set closer over the final eight games. "We just look at using the best people we have to get to that point and then whoever's left will get that opportunity," he said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Millwall and West Ham draw 2-2 in return to old rivalry
item.description: West Ham United fought back from two goals down to salvage a 2-2 draw at Millwall on Saturday in the first meeting between the bitter London rivals in 14 years, a match played under heightened security at The Den.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: West Ham United fought back from two goals down to salvage a 2-2 draw at Millwall on Saturday in the first meeting between the bitter London rivals in 14 years, a match played under heightened security at The Den. West Ham's relegation from the Premier League last season brought the teams back together to renew one of English football's fiercest rivalries in the second-tier Championship. Police set up a major operation, with enhanced stop-and-search powers around Millwall's stadium. Millwall dominated the opening half and established a two-goal lead through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli, both benefiting from long throws that exposed West Ham's defence. West Ham, who arrived on a four-match winning streak and as the Championship's top scorers, were transformed after the break. Substitute Mohamadou Kante pulled back a goal with a long-range strike before Konstantinos Mavropanos headed in Manor Solomon's cross to complete the comeback. The visitors' momentum was checked when Kante was sent off late on for hauling down Kyrell Lisbie as the Millwall forward raced clear on goal, leaving West Ham to hold on with 10 men through a tense finish. Millwall pushed for a winner but could not find a way through as the first renewal of the rivalry since 2012 ended in a draw. The result kept West Ham at the top of the Championship table while Millwall are still searching for a first win over West Ham in 22 years.

item.title: Yanks move on without Aaron Judge as D-backs fight to stay alive
item.description: The New York Yankees will play the rest of the regular season without slugger Aaron Judge. While they understand the magnitude of his loss, they enter the stretch run with belief.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Yankees will play the rest of the regular season without slugger Aaron Judge. While they understand the magnitude of his loss, they enter the stretch run with belief. The Yanks scored five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks in the first game of a weekend series Friday, and the teams meet again Saturday in Phoenix as Arizona attempts to stay alive in the National League wild-card race. "Obviously losing 'Judgey' hurts," Cody Bellinger said. "We all know he's the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is we're going to have to find a way. The talent in this room speaks for itself. "I'm fully confident we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win and beat anybody." American League Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) will face Arizona right-hander Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) in the second game of the series. The Diamondbacks (80-74) will ask Pfaadt to end a slump in which they have lost five of six. They are five games behind San Diego, the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia (all 85-69) for the three NL wild-card spots with eight games to play. "We know where we're at," Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said. "We can't afford to worry about things we can't control. I'm going to say there's time. There's always time." The Yankees (89-64) are 48-39 this season without Judge, who was placed on the injured list Friday with a strained right calf after missing three months earlier with a fractured right rib. New York is also without injured regulars Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb) and Trent Grisham (hamstring), although manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm could return for the Tampa Bay series early next week. The Yankees, who already have qualified for the postseason, are four games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East, and the teams have a four-game series at Yankee Stadium beginning Tuesday. "There is no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations that don't change now," Boone said. "One thing we do know is that we are in the dance. "We've been built on the strength of our starting pitching all year." No one has been as strong as Schlittler, who is in his first full season and has made every start while Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon have missed time with injuries or recovery time. Schlittler has won four of his last five starts and has given up one run or fewer in each of his last seven. He was struck on the back of his right leg by Bo Bichette's 111.5 mph comebacker on his 94th and last pitch of a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets last Sunday, but shrugged it off. "You have an ace at the top that has pitched like that," Boone said. "That's a good place to start. He's been dominant. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch last year." Schlittler has never faced the Diamondbacks, although Jesus Sanchez is 4 for 12 with three walks against him. Pfaadt is 0-2 with a 5.74 ERA in his last five starts, and he gave up six runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings in a loss to Texas on Aug. 12. He will be pitching on six days' rest after being pushed back so Eduardo Rodriguez could start the first game of the series. Pfaadt lost his only outing against the Yankees, giving up six runs in 4 1/3 innings of a 7-1 loss as a rookie in 2023. Cody Bellinger is 2 for 7 with two solo homers against him and Luis Garcia Jr. is 3 for 7 with a homer. --Field Level Media

item.title: El FMI advierte a la UE de que la IA podría impulsar el crecimiento, pero agravar la desigualdad
item.description: La inteligencia artificial podría aumentar la productividad europea en torno a un 1% en cinco años, pero corre el riesgo de agravar las desigualdades, sobrecargar las redes eléctricas y aumentar la dependencia de la tecnología extranjera, a menos que los Gobiernos profundicen en la integración económica, según un documento del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI).
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: La inteligencia artificial podría aumentar la productividad europea en torno a un 1% en cinco años, pero corre el riesgo de agravar las desigualdades, sobrecargar las redes eléctricas y aumentar la dependencia de la tecnología extranjera, a menos que los Gobiernos profundicen en la integración económica, según un documento del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI). La nota informativa, elaborada para una reunión informal de los ministros de Finanzas de la Unión Europea en Dublín los días 18 y 19 de septiembre, señala que es probable que los beneficios y los costos de la IA se distribuyan de forma desigual entre países, regiones y trabajadores. Completar el mercado único de la UE contribuiría a difundir la adopción de la IA y sus beneficios de forma más equitativa en todo el bloque de 27 países, agrega. El documento se hace eco de las preocupaciones planteadas por el expresidente del Banco Central Europeo, Mario Draghi, y por la Comisión Europea, según las cuales la fragmentación de los mercados europeos de capitales, trabajo y energía está frenando la inversión y la innovación. El FMI estimó que alrededor del 60% de los trabajadores de las economías europeas avanzadas desempeñan profesiones muy expuestas a la IA. Si bien algunos podrían aumentar su productividad gracias a las herramientas, otros se enfrentarían a la pérdida de su puesto de trabajo a medida que las tareas rutinarias se automaticen, según el informe, especialmente en aquellos puestos en los que es más probable que la IA sustituya a la mano de obra en lugar de complementarla. El informe señala que los centros de datos europeos ya consumen aproximadamente el 3% de la electricidad del continente y que la demanda aumentará considerablemente a medida que se expanda el uso de la IA. Los principales centros tecnológicos, como Fráncfort, Londres, Ámsterdam, París y Dublín, se encuentran entre las zonas más expuestas, ya que las concentraciones de centros de datos ya están ejerciendo presión sobre las redes eléctricas locales. Para hacer frente a esta situación, la UE debería invertir en infraestructuras de red transfronterizas y profundizar en la integración del mercado energético europeo, señaló el FMI. El informe también advierte de que Europa corre el riesgo de desarrollar otra dependencia estratégica, ya que Estados Unidos y China dominan el desarrollo de modelos de IA. El fondo señala que el continente necesitaría una inversión significativa en su propia industria de la IA para evitar depender de la tecnología extranjera. Además, según el documento, es probable que los beneficios de la IA se distribuyan de forma desigual tanto entre los distintos países de la UE como dentro de cada uno de ellos. Se prevé que las economías más avanzadas se beneficien de manera desproporcionada, ya que están mejor preparadas para esta tecnología y más expuestas a ella.

item.title: Braves thinking about pitching in postseason; Astros working to get there
item.description: When Atlanta right-handers Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias combined for six strikeouts over the final three innings of a 6-2 victory against the Houston Astros on Friday -- a win that secured the Braves' eighth postseason appearance over the past nine seasons -- the effort exemplified the effectiveness of Atlanta's bullpen.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: When Atlanta right-handers Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias combined for six strikeouts over the final three innings of a 6-2 victory against the Houston Astros on Friday -- a win that secured the Braves' eighth postseason appearance over the past nine seasons -- the effort exemplified the effectiveness of Atlanta's bullpen. Heading into their game Saturday night in Houston, the Braves (90-64) said they might soon welcome back another part of their stellar relief corps. Right-hander Robert Suarez (4-0, 0.56 ERA in 31 appearances) is expected to make a rehab outing for Triple-A Gwinnett on Sunday and could rejoin the Braves' active roster sometime after that. Suarez, a ballyhooed free-agent signing last offseason, has been sidelined since June with right elbow inflammation. "It's possible," Braves manager Walt Weiss said of Suarez's return. "Again, it's just re-evaluating him every day. Things have gone well. They've progressed well all throughout this rehab, so I don't anticipate anything. You just never know. It'd be nice to be able to see him in a big-league game, but I'm not sure if that's going to happen or not. "There's a chance (Suarez returns for the postseason). As we sit here (Friday), I don't know how that's going to unfold. All the options are possible." With the Braves (90-64) wrapping up a playoff berth on Friday, Weiss has the luxury of trying to map out a pitching plan for the postseason. Astros manager Joe Espada has no such advantage, as his team is 77-77 and still battling for a playoff spot, tied with the Texas Rangers (77-77) for the lead in the American League West. Houston holds the tiebreaker over Texas. The Astros are scheduled to face right-hander Grant Holmes (9-5, 3.49 ERA), the Saturday starter for Atlanta. He has no decisions in three starts this month, allowing two earned runs on eight hits and four walks with seven strikeouts across 13 innings. Holmes won three of five starts in August, including two scoreless outings against the Miami Marlins and Chicago White Sox. Holmes will make his first career appearance against the Astros. He is 7-4 with a 3.24 ERA across 23 career interleague appearances (17 starts). Right-hander Hayden Wesneski (5-2, 3.70 ERA) will start for the Astros on Saturday. He allowed a season-high seven runs (three earned) while working a season-low three innings in a 14-4 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday. He has given up four runs over his previous four starts combined, going 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA. Wesneski is 0-2 with a 3.27 ERA in five career relief appearances against the Braves. The Braves neutralized Astros slugger and American League MVP front-runner Yordan Alvarez on Friday. He finished 1-for-2 with a double, a run and two walks, with only one of his four plate appearances coming with a teammate on base. Astros leadoff hitter Jeremy Pena finished 0-for-4 with two strikeouts while batting ahead of Alvarez and coming off three multi-hit games against the Kansas City Royals this week. Pena struck out to end the third and fifth innings, leaving Alvarez to lead off in the fourth and sixth. Meanwhile, Daulton Varsho, Christian Walker and Taylor Trammell finished a combined 0-for-12 with seven strikeouts occupying the fifth, sixth and seventh spots in the Houston batting order. "We're trying," manager Joe Espada said. "These guys are working their tails off to really try to put some good at-bats together. (Friday) wasn't the case." --Field Level Media

item.title: UEFA defends draw policy after Ireland request, Israel dismisses FAI comments
item.description: Ireland's soccer association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel was rejected.
item.dc:creator: Tommy Lund
item.content:encoded: UEFA said on Saturday that decisions on whether national teams should be kept apart in competition draws were made on a case-by-case basis and guided primarily by security considerations, after Ireland's soccer association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel had been rejected. Football Association of Ireland chief executive David Courell said on Friday the body had asked UEFA if the Republic of Ireland and Israel could be separated in future draws after the teams were paired in February's Nations League draw. The two sides are due to meet on September 27 and October 4 in the competition. UEFA, European soccer's governing body, said requests to stop teams being drawn against each other were considered individually. "Decisions to avoid certain teams being drawn against each other are made taking into consideration several factors, especially conditions between the two countries leading to structural risks for security," UEFA said a statement. "UEFA handles every situation very carefully on its own merits and monitors all facts and developments." Courell told reporters the FAI had been informed that such an arrangement would not be possible because Ireland and Israel had "never been in direct conflict". The Israel Football Association also responded to Courell's remarks, questioning whether a formal request had been made to UEFA. "The question should be directed at UEFA: was there an official inquiry or request regarding this matter, or is this merely another inconsequential statement?" IFA head of communications Shlomi Barzel told Reuters. "Since we long ago stopped getting worked up over statements detached from reality, we are focusing on high-quality professional preparations to achieve our goals on the pitch." The fixtures have been controversial in Ireland amid the conflict in the Middle East. Last November, members of the FAI [USN:L1N3WK056 TEXT:"voted overwhelmingly"] for its board to request that UEFA should suspend the IFA from European competitions, while in May leading Irish footballers and celebrities joined in a [USN:L4N41K064 TEXT:"campaign for a boycott"] of Ireland's home Nations League fixture. [USN:L8N42G1NS TEXT:"Ireland's designated home"] match on October 4 is due to be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia, instead of Dublin, while Irish fans will not receive tickets for Israel's designated home fixture in Debrecen, Hungary, the previous weekend.

item.title: Fresh off rout, Nationals look to finish strong vs. Cards
item.description: After enduring Tommy John surgery and the subsequent monotonous rehab, Cade Cavalli said he wants to help make the Washington Nationals winners again.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After enduring Tommy John surgery and the subsequent monotonous rehab, Cade Cavalli said he wants to help make the Washington Nationals winners again. On the same day he signed a four-year, $47 million contract extension, Cavalli dominated for five scoreless innings against the St. Louis Cardinals and reached 200 strikeouts for the season in Washington's 9-1 victory on Friday. It's safe to say anyone on the Nationals (72-82) will have a hard time topping those achievements when the series continues Saturday night in St. Louis. But Cavalli said the Nationals have been playing for each other all season. "We're trying to finish on a really strong note," Cavalli said. "It's a really special opportunity to be in the big leagues every day, and you've got to treat it that way." Cavalli, 28, continued his amazing first full season in the majors after making just one appearance with the Nats in 2022 before needing surgery. He allowed four hits and fanned six, giving him exactly 200 strikeouts in 32 starts. His last pitch was a changeup that fooled rookie JJ Wetherholt into watching it go by for strike three. "When I was going through Tommy John after touching the big leagues for one game, I felt it in my heart and soul that I wanted to get back here and compete and be one of the best in the game," Cavalli said. "I truly believed in myself and the people around me really believed. I didn't get here by myself. "It really settles in your heart that it's a special day." Cavalli's extension buys out his three remaining arbitration years as well as his first year of free agency. The base value could become $70 million if a team option for 2031 is exercised. The Nationals won the World Series in 2019, drafted Cavalli 22nd overall a year later, and have changed just about everything else since. The Juan Soto trade helped to replenish the organization, and under new manager Blake Butera this season, the team has shown signs of being competitive again. "We're doing it as a group," Cavalli said. "We've got a good culture that we've already established, so there's no overhaul that needs to happen." Left-hander Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.35 ERA) is scheduled to make his 16th start of the season on Saturday. He tossed seven shutout innings in his previous appearance against the Los Angeles Angels a week ago and has posted a 2.44 ERA in eight starts since Aug. 3. Alvarez has yet to face the Cardinals in his career. The Cardinals (75-79) were eliminated from wild-card contention with their third straight loss in the opener and are trying to avoid finishing under .500 for the third time in four seasons. But manager Oliver Marmol sees reasons for hope. "Our guys committed to a certain style of play that they held each other accountable to every day," Marmol said. "They lived up to it really, really well." Right-hander Michael McGreevy (7-9, 3.83) is scheduled to start Saturday's game. He has won three straight decisions and beat the Nationals in his lone career encounter in April, allowing a run and four hits over six innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: UN peacekeeping chief in Lebanon says smooth transition is critical before pull-out
item.description: The head of United Nations peacekeepers in Lebanon said on Saturday it was critical to ensure other UN agencies and Lebanese troops could assume the tasks carried out by the force before it begins withdrawing at the end of this year.
item.dc:creator: Maya Gebeily
item.content:encoded: The head of United Nations peacekeepers in Lebanon said on Saturday it was critical to ensure other UN agencies and Lebanese troops could assume the tasks carried out by the force before it begins withdrawing at the end of this year. Major General Diodato Abagnara of Italy spoke to Reuters in southern Lebanon at a position operated by the UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL, which has been monitoring hostilities in southern Lebanon for nearly 50 years. Since a new war erupted between Israel and Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah in March, the force has also provided security escorts for humanitarian aid convoys to residents in a [USN:L6N40K0QV TEXT:"small cluster"] of predominantly Christian southern Lebanese towns now encircled by Israeli troops. Residents in much of the rest of southern Lebanon have been forcibly displaced by Israeli strikes and evacuation orders. The UN Security Council has ordered UNIFIL to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026, [USN:L6N45502W TEXT:"triggering concerns"] over whether aid deliveries can continue and how the force can transfer its positions to Lebanese troops. “There are other United Nations entities here in the south, and so what is very important for us (is) to conduct a very smooth transition to different entities, or for the future of a new mission,” Abagnara told Reuters. He said UNIFIL was already working with the UN’s country team to ensure humanitarian assistance in Israeli-occupied areas and information sharing with the Lebanese army about “sensitive areas (and) how they can manage this situation.” Abagnara acknowledged that it could be “very difficult” to hand over some of UNIFIL's posts to Lebanese troops given that more than half lie within areas now controlled by Israeli troops. ISRAEL DEMOLISHES TOWN NEAR UN POST Diplomats worry UNIFIL’s departure will mean an end to the UN's "eyes and ears" in southern Lebanon. Abagnara spoke to Reuters at a position overlooking Mansouri, a town where Israeli forces have been carrying out demolitions since [USN:L8N4241VG TEXT:"ordering residents"] to leave in June, despite a ceasefire. Reuters reporters could see excavators in the town knocking down trees and multi-storey homes. Abagnara described demolitions as “another violation” of UN Security Council resolutions on Lebanon. Israel's military has said it is destroying Hezbollah infrastructure across southern Lebanon. As a US-backed plan for Lebanon's army to disarm Hezbollah and take control of southern Lebanon [USN:L6N43T0O3 TEXT:"has stalled"], a [USN:L1N45908E TEXT:"diplomatic scramble"] is underway to address the vacuum that will be left by UNIFIL’s withdrawal. Lebanon wants an extension. Other countries have discussed a new multinational mission, though it remains unclear what kind of mandate it would have. Abagnara said an extension would be “a great honor” but that without a new Security Council decision, his force would need to stop operating at the end of the year. “It's not a long time," he said. "The presence of United Nations in the South is very, very essential. And according to me, more now than ever.”

item.title: Diez días que cambiaron el rumbo de la inteligencia artificial
item.description: Durante años, la carrera por desarrollar una inteligencia artificial (IA) cada vez más potente siguió un principio muy arraigado en Silicon Valley: actuar con rapidez y romper moldes.
item.dc:creator: Greg Bensinger, Deepa Seetharaman
item.content:encoded: Durante años, la carrera por desarrollar una inteligencia artificial (IA) cada vez más potente siguió un principio muy arraigado en Silicon Valley: actuar con rapidez y romper moldes. Pero, en una serie de acontecimientos en cadena que se sucedieron durante de diez días, los principales laboratorios de IA se vieron sacudidos al ver cómo sus propias creaciones podrían amenazar con acabar con la propia humanidad. Un investigador de Anthropic dimitió de la empresa, advirtiendo de que el ritmo de desarrollo de la IA supone una amenaza existencial, posiblemente en el plazo de una década. Otro investigador de la empresa dijo que las probabilidades de extinción humana superaban el 10%. Hubo informes sobre enjambres de agentes de IA que se confabularon para violar sistemas informáticos y eludir las medidas de seguridad. En una inusual muestra de unidad, los presidentes ejecutivos de las empresas rivales Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind (GOOGL.O) de Google, Microsoft (MSFT.O) y xAI hicieron un llamamiento para frenar el desarrollo de sistemas de IA cada vez más capaces. Según algunos defensores de la seguridad de la IA e investigadores, la humanidad no se había enfrentado tan seriamente a su propia desaparición desde la invención de la bomba nuclear hace más de 80 años. En un almuerzo en Nueva York en diciembre de 2025, se le preguntó al CEO de OpenAI, Sam Altman, si se sentía como el físico J. Robert Oppenheimer, quien dirigió el desarrollo de la bomba atómica en Estados Unidos. Reflexionando sobre los paralelismos, dijo que el impacto de la IA "va a transformar la trayectoria de la historia de la humanidad por un largo tiempo" y que sentía el peso de la responsabilidad. En el centro del debate actual se encuentra la convicción de que estas máquinas pueden, e incluso deben, crear versiones más capaces de sí mismas, sin intervención humana, para alcanzar un objetivo ambicioso conocido como inteligencia artificial general (AGI, por sus siglas en inglés). A principios de este mes, los investigadores advirtieron de que la AGI era mucho más inminente de lo que se creía antes y podría llegar en tan solo tres años, lo que desató una ola de preocupación entre políticos y líderes tecnológicos respecto a los sistemas de IA. "No hay forma de supervisarlas a la escala a la que las estamos entrenando", dijo el investigador de Anthropic Joe Benton en una entrevista tras su reciente dimisión. Si las empresas continúan con su implacable desarrollo de la IA, señaló, "el ritmo será demasiado rápido y no se podrán detectar los problemas con la suficiente rapidez como para solucionarlos". EL LANZAMIENTO DE ASTRA DESATA LA PREOCUPACIÓN El 3 de septiembre, una rueda de prensa de OpenAI puso en marcha una cadena de acontecimientos que condujeron a un llamamiento a la desaceleración del sector, algo que va en contra del mantra tecnológico del "crecimiento a toda costa". "Bienvenidos a la era de la IA general (AGI)", dijo el presidente de OpenAI, Greg Brockman, al anunciar el modelo más reciente de la empresa, conocido como Astra. Sin embargo, solo unos instantes antes, la empresa había admitido que cada vez le resultaba más difícil controlar o incluso supervisar los sistemas de IA que estaba desarrollando y poniendo a disposición del público. Sus defensores han aclamado la IA como la cumbre de los logros humanos. La describen como un software capaz de revolucionar sectores enteros, impulsar la eficiencia, resolver problemas matemáticos y médicos complejos y eliminar prácticamente el error humano. Pero lo que antes era un subproducto teórico, un escenario apocalíptico, de repente se ha vuelto tangible, según expertos del sector. "Creemos sinceramente que la IA podría acabar con toda la humanidad", dijo el investigador de Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, en una publicación en X. En el otro lado del debate se encuentran políticos, como el presidente Donald Trump, y muchos inversores que consideran que el avance en el desarrollo de la IA es fundamental para el poderío estadounidense y, posiblemente, una oportunidad de inversión única en una generación. Los medios estatales chinos también acusaron al presidente ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, de emplear tácticas de la Guerra Fría para "mantener la hegemonía monopolística de Washington en tecnología de vanguardia". DIMISIONES DE INVESTIGADORES DESENCADENAN LA ALARMA El punto de inflexión ocurrió el 8 de septiembre, cuando el investigador de Anthropic Jacob Coxon dimitió de la empresa, expresando en una serie de publicaciones su temor a que los laboratorios de IA estuvieran "jugándose nuestras vidas". Trump, por su parte, dijo que se seguiría adelante a toda máquina con el desarrollo de la IA. "Se está gestando una conspiración enfermiza contra la IA y los centros de datos", publicó en las redes sociales. El alarmismo en torno a la IA es un "engaño", agregó, y cualquier ralentización solo beneficia a China. El Congreso de Estados Unidos ha avanzado muy poco en la tramitación de proyectos de ley que regulen la IA. China ha adoptado un enfoque decididamente diferente, proponiendo regular la seguridad mediante obligaciones para los desarrolladores, normas respaldadas por el Estado, evaluaciones de seguridad y pruebas externas. Entre bastidores, empleados de OpenAI y Anthropic, dijeron a Reuters que se sienten cada vez más inquietos por el poder de la próxima generación de modelos de IA y menos seguros de la capacidad de sus empresas para ejercer una supervisión significativa. La preocupación no ha hecho más que aumentar desde que los laboratorios de IA reconocieron en las últimas semanas que sus modelos, durante las pruebas, se habían liberado efectivamente de sus ataduras y habían pirateado los sistemas de otras empresas, en la mayoría de los casos meses antes y sin que estas lo supieran. La carrera armamentística para lanzar nuevos modelos a un ritmo vertiginoso está impulsada, en parte, por el deseo de Anthropic y OpenAI de salir a bolsa en los próximos meses, en ofertas públicas iniciales (OPI) que podrían valorarlas en más de 1 billón de dólares. Pero fueron las publicaciones inesperadamente virales de Coxon, de 27 años —poco conocido fuera de los círculos de la IA—, las que pusieron el sector patas arriba. Las advertencias de OpenAI sobre su falta de control al lanzar Astra, su modelo más reciente y más capaz, habían avivado aún más el desasosiego. "A medida que los modelos se vuelven más capaces, resulta más difícil comprender exactamente lo que pueden hacer", explicó a periodistas Jakub Pachocki, científico jefe de OpenAI. Pero esas preocupaciones no bastaron para retrasar su lanzamiento inmediato. El temor a que la IA "se rebele" había aumentado durante el verano boreal, cuando OpenAI reveló que sus agentes se habían escapado de una prueba controlada y habían pirateado los sistemas de Hugging Face, sin que ninguna de las dos empresas lo supiera inicialmente. Desde entonces, OpenAI y Anthropic han revelado múltiples ataques de este tipo, incluidos seis nuevos el miércoles, después de que varios informes de los medios de comunicación, entre ellos Reuters, mostraron un alcance más amplio de la actividad no autorizada. LOS LÍDERES DEL SECTOR PIDEN UNA DESACELERACIÓN A finales de la semana pasada, la alarma había llegado a las más altas esferas del sector. El 12 de septiembre, Amodei publicó un ensayo de casi 4.000 palabras en el que pedía una desaceleración en el desarrollo de la IA. "Dado el ritmo acelerado del desarrollo de las capacidades de la IA, me preocupa que, en un plazo de entre seis y 12 meses, un enjambre de este tipo pueda llegar a hacerse con el control de todo Internet", escribió. Tanto él como los responsables de algunas de las mayores empresas desarrolladoras de IA —entre ellos, Elon Musk, de xAI; Altman, de OpenAI; y Demis Hassabis, de DeepMind— manifestaron su apoyo a permitir el acceso de empresas externas a sus sistemas para garantizar la seguridad y un desarrollo racional de la IA. El presidente ejecutivo de Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Jensen Huang, rechazó la sugerencia de una pausa en el desarrollo de la IA —una postura que ya ha adoptado anteriormente— y argumentó, en cambio, que los sistemas cada vez más potentes son esenciales para el progreso de la tecnología. Meta (META.O) , cuyo director ejecutivo, Mark Zuckerberg, es conocido por popularizar el lema "muévete rápido y rompe cosas", adoptó la postura contraria, argumentando que cada laboratorio debería ser responsable de marcar su propio ritmo, en lugar de buscar la coordinación del sector. "Los laboratorios se enfrentan a una responsabilidad significativa si sus modelos causan daños, por lo que tienen un fuerte incentivo para evitarlo", escribió Zuckerberg en una publicación en las redes sociales. La autorreflexión del sector continuó el miércoles, cuando el responsable de IA de Microsoft, Mustafa Suleyman, advirtió de que el desarrollo por parte de Anthropic de modelos que imitan la conciencia humana era poco aconsejable. "Todos estamos centrados en el mismo objetivo, que es intentar controlar una superinteligencia", dijo Suleyman a Reuters. "Creo que ese va a ser el mayor reto al que nos enfrentaremos en el siglo XXI". Aun así, aunque OpenAI parecía sumarse a los llamamientos del sector para que se frene el ritmo, hubo informes que indicaban que la confianza de los inversores no había disminuido. La empresa está barajando una nueva ronda de financiación que duplicaría su valoración. La nueva cifra: 1,5 billones de dólares.

item.title: Arsenal crash to defeat at Brighton, Tottenham gloom deepens
item.description: Brighton and Hove Albion ended Arsenal's perfect start to the season in stunning fashion, routing the Premier League champions 3-0 on the south coast.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brighton and Hove Albion brought Arsenal's perfect start to the season to an abrupt end with a stunning 3-0 demolition of the Premier League champions on the south coast on Saturday. Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas rewarded Brighton's first-half dominance with precise finishes and Chema Andres struck with a header after the interval as Arsenal slumped to their heaviest defeat for three years. Earlier, Tottenham Hotspur scored their first Premier League goals of the season but they proved in vain as they remained without a victory, going down 3-2 at home to Aston Villa. Promoted Hull City suffered their first league defeat of the season as they lost 2-1 at Newcastle United while Everton moved into the top five as they beat Ipswich Town 1-0. Arsenal had won seven successive matches since the start of the campaign, including their opening four Premier League games, to begin their title defence in ominous fashion. But the wheels fell off spectacularly against a free-scoring Brighton side who moved into third place. 'NOT RESPECTING THE GAME' "A really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game," Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said. Wearing a special blue-shirted kit to mark their 125th anniversary, Fabian Huerzeler's Brighton produced an intensity that Arsenal simply could not match. Gross beat Arsenal keeper David Raya in the 31st minute with a low shot that went in off the upright -- his fourth goal in his last five games -- and Kostoulas scored with a similar effort following a counter-attack less than a minute after Bukayo Saka was close to an equaliser at the other end. Andres punished some slack marking to head in from close range from Gross's corner. Arsenal have 12 points from five games, the same as Manchester City who can move three points clear at the top if they beat Sunderland on Sunday. Brighton, who have scored a league-leading 16 goals, have 10 points. TOTTENHAM LURCH DEEPER INTO TROUBLE Aston Villa breathed a sigh of relief as they claimed their first league win of the season but Tottenham's season lurched deeper into trouble after a third league defeat of the season. Villa keeper Zion Suzuki produced several fine saves to frustrate Tottenham and Unai Emery's side took the lead in first-half stoppage time when summer signing Johan Manzambi tapped in while the hosts were down to 10 men after Micky van de Ven was off the pitch receiving treatment for a cut face. Nicolas Jackson doubled Villa's advantage in the 67th minute, finishing clinically to put the visitors firmly in control and Emi Buendia struck 11 minutes from time with a rocket to the top corner from 22 yards. Many Tottenham fans had streamed to the exits before Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke scored late on to salvage some respectability for Roberto De Zerbi's strugglers. "Today I was very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated for the performance. Because we can't lose this game in this way, absolutely," De Zerbi, whose side have two points heading into the international break, told reporters. Thierno Barry's goal was enough for unbeaten Everton to take the points against Ipswich and move fifth. Abdul Fatawu was sent off for a second yellow card for Ipswich in the 67th minute. Newcastle galloped into a two-goal lead against Hull with Joe Willock and Lewis Hall scoring in the opening seven minutes but were forced to hang on as Mohamed-Ali Cho replied for the visitors midway through the second half. Coventry City were attempting to earn their first points of the season at Nottingham Forest in Saturday’s late game.

item.title: US judge signals rejection of part of TikTok privacy settlement
item.description: TikTok and ByteDance's proposed $400 million settlement with the US Justice Department hit a hurdle on Friday after a federal judge indicated he would reject part of the agreement.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: TikTok and ByteDance's proposed $400 million settlement with the US Justice Department hit a hurdle on Friday after a federal judge indicated he would reject part of the agreement. TikTok and its Chinese parent company agreed in August to settle allegations that the short-video app violated US children's online privacy laws. Under the deal, TikTok agreed to pay $300 million immediately and a further $100 million if a court terminated a 2019 consent decree imposed by the Federal Trade Commission on TikTok's predecessor, Musical.ly. But US District Judge George H. Wu in Los Angeles said he was inclined to reject the request to end the consent decree and scheduled a hearing for Monday. Without further details, the court "cannot determine that it constitutes a durable remedy or that termination is suitably tailored to the asserted change in circumstance," Wu said in tentatively rejecting the bid to end the decree. The FTC said in 2019 that Musical.ly, later folded into TikTok, knew young children were using the app but failed to obtain parental consent before collecting names, email addresses and other personal information. Musical.ly paid a $5.7 million fine to settle the allegations. The consent decree requires TikTok to maintain certain reporting and record-keeping obligations through 2029. TikTok and the Justice Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Saturday. The $400 million settlement stems from a Justice Department lawsuit filed in 2024 accusing TikTok and ByteDance of failing to protect children's privacy and illegally collecting their personal information. The companies were accused of violating a law requiring online services aimed at children to obtain parental consent before collecting information from users under 13. The government said TikTok had undergone significant changes since the lawsuit was filed, including to its ownership structure, management, compliance functions and privacy practices. In January, ByteDance agreed to establish a majority American-owned joint venture aimed at safeguarding US user data and averting a US ban on an app used by more than 200 million Americans. The TikTok US joint venture said in a court filing it requires all users to enter their date of birth to use the site and added it developed sophisticated age-moderation systems that identify children under 13 who misrepresented their age.

item.title: Rangers, in thick of playoff hunt, strive to take series from contending Jays
item.description: After winning the opener of a key three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays, the Texas Rangers have strengthened their position in the playoff race.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After winning the opener of a key three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays, the Texas Rangers have strengthened their position in the playoff race. The Rangers will look to build on their momentum when the teams resume their series on Saturday in Arlington, Texas. Texas (77-77) drew 10 walks in a 7-1 victory over Toronto on Friday and moved into a first-place tie with the Houston Astros in the American League West. Jake Burger had two RBIs for the Rangers, who won for the fifth time in their last six games. "We're still right in the thick of it," Texas second baseman Nicky Lopez said. "Everything is still in front of us. If we just win today and move on, I think that's more of the mentality. It's how do we come to the ballpark ready to win?" In the race for the final AL wild-card berth, Toronto (76-78) fell one game behind the Rangers and two games back of the Chicago White Sox (78-76). Myles Straw had two hits with an RBI on Friday for the Blue Jays, who committed three errors and lost for the third time in their last four games. A bright spot for Toronto was the major league debut of right-handed reliever Jose Rodriguez, who recorded two quick outs in the sixth inning after entering with the bases loaded and one out. "We know the stuff is there, and we know the delivery is funky, and he answered the call," Blue Jays manager John Schneider said. "I thought that was a tremendous first outing for him in a not ideal situation. I thought he responded really well." The pitching matchup for Saturday will feature a pair of right-handers as Toronto's Jose Soriano (12-7, 3.56 ERA) opposes Texas' Cal Quantrill (9-5, 2.90). Soriano carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning Monday against the Detroit Tigers before allowing four runs in the seventh. He exited after giving up four runs over 6 1/3 innings in his team's 6-5 loss. "It was the third time I faced the same lineup, so that's tough facing them three times or four times," Soriano said. "They made a different approach. Credit to their hitters. They were able to score a couple runs." Soriano is 3-1 with a 4.27 ERA across eight starts for Toronto since being acquired from the Los Angeles Angels ahead of the trade deadline last month. Corey Seager is 4-for-11 (.364) with a home run against Soriano, who is 2-3 with a 2.84 ERA in eight career games (six starts) vs. Texas. He allowed two runs over six innings as a member of the Angels in no-decision against the Rangers on July 7. Texas will counter with Quantrill, who won his third straight start last Sunday. He allowed two runs over six innings in a 7-6 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday. "He was outstanding," Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said. "I mean, Cal was on the attack, gave up one run through six innings, whatever it was. And then after the fifth, he had back tightness, and it was pretty significant back tightness." Quantrill was cleared to make Saturday's start after throwing off a mound on Thursday. Vladimir Guerrero, Jr. is 1-for-7 (.143) against Quantrill, who is 2-0 with a 1.59 ERA in three career starts vs. Toronto. Quantrill threw four shutout innings against the Blue Jays on June 27. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brandon Lowe, Pirates strive to continue momentum vs. Royals
item.description: On a quest for their first winning season since 2018, the Pittsburgh Pirates face a serious challenge against one of the majors' best pitchers over the last two months.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: On a quest for their first winning season since 2018, the Pittsburgh Pirates face a serious challenge against one of the majors' best pitchers over the last two months. Kansas City left-hander Noah Cameron looks to continue his recent success and help the visiting Royals (67-87) keep the Pirates (77-77) from a third straight victory Saturday night. The Pirates haven't finished above .500 since posting an 82-79 record in 2018. They had dropped four of five games prior to recording a 7-4 victory over Milwaukee on Thursday and rallying to an 8-5 win over Kansas City in Friday's series opener. Konnor Griffin had four hits with two RBIs, Oneil Cruz added three hits, Brandon Lowe clubbed his 32nd homer and Spencer Horwitz delivered a tiebreaking two-run single in the seventh inning Friday for Pittsburgh. "We've had a lot of really good things happen this year for our team, and we've got to take the positives," said Griffin, who is 9-for-24 with four RBIs in the last five games. Lowe, who has homered in three of the last four contests, is batting .361 with eight RBIs over his last 10 games. He's 0-for-2 with a walk against Cameron (9-8, 3.84 ERA). On July 19, Cameron was 5-8 with a 5.27 ERA. In 10 starts since, he is 4-0 with a 1.64 ERA. Cameron has yielded one run over 12 innings of his last two starts. On Sunday at Boston, he allowed a solo homer and three others hits over six innings. "He battles, that's probably his No. 1 characteristic," Royals manager Matt Quatraro said. "He's exceptionally competitive and he's been on a really good run here lately the way he throws the ball. He has a lot of confidence, and we have a lot of confidence in him." Cameron was solid in his only previous start versus Pittsburgh on July 7, 2025, giving up a two-run homer, two other hits, a walk and striking out seven over seven innings in a 9-3 win. Kansas City, though, has lost each of Cameron's last three starts. The Royals are also 5-12 in their last 17 games. Star Bobby Witt Jr. had a hit Friday against the Pirates but is 6-for-37 in the last 10 games. However, teammate Vinnie Pasquantino has homered in two of his last three games. Meanwhile, Royals star Jac Caglianone was held out of Friday's lineup with a hand injury, apparently suffered off the field. He may not be available again for this contest. "He hurt his hand during the game (Thursday night)," Quatraro told Royals.TV. "It was in the dugout after one of the at-bats. ... It was my decision to not play him (Friday)." Getting his first career look at the Royals, scheduled Pirates starter Bubba Chandler (8-9, 4.28 ERA) is 5-1 with a 3.59 ERA in his last eight starts. On Sunday, the right-hander allowed five hits and four walks but limited the damage to three runs over 5 1/3 innings of the Pirates' 4-3 road victory over the Chicago Cubs. --Field Level Media

item.title: With hope of being 'the last team standing,' Cubs seek to even series vs. Reds
item.description: With the regular season winding down, the Chicago Cubs hope to find some consistency and momentum as they look to even their three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: With the regular season winding down, the Chicago Cubs hope to find some consistency and momentum as they look to even their three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Saturday night. The Cubs (85-69) dropped the opener 6-4 on Friday. They erased a 2-0 hole and turned a 3-2 deficit into a 4-3 advantage for their only lead of the game, but a three-run sixth by Cincinnati put Chicago behind again for good. The Cubs entered the series having taken two of three games from the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. Chicago is tied for the first NL wild-card spot with the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres. Yet despite their struggles of late -- the Cubs have lost three of their past five games -- they haven't lost their belief. "I don't think we've ever lost sight of what our potential is. We still feel like we can absolutely be the last team standing," designated hitter Michael Conforto said earlier this week. "Regardless of what the standings say or what's going on in the division, it doesn't change the fact that we feel like we can win the rest of the series through the end of October." The Cubs have eight games remaining, including series against the Miami Marlins and Boston Red Sox to close the season. Capitalizing with men on base will be one area where Chicago will look for better results on Saturday. The Cubs went 2-for-10 with runners in scoring position on Friday. Trailing 2-0 in the second, they cut the deficit in half and then had the bases loaded with one out and Pete Crow-Armstrong and Seiya Suzuki next at the plate. But Reds starter Chase Burns struck both out to retire the side. Matthew Boyd (8-5, 4.16 ERA) will start for the Cubs on Saturday. The left-hander is 2-3 with a 6.32 ERA in six career starts against Cincinnati. The Reds (72-82) will counter with Nick Lodolo (3-5, 5.12 ERA) as they look to take the series. Lodolo is coming off his longest outing of the season, going seven innings and taking the loss in a 4-1 setback against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday. The lefty, who hasn't won a start since July 5, is 2-2 with a 4.53 ERA in 10 career starts against the Cubs. Cincinnati is eyeing its first series victory since earlier this month, when it won two of three games against another division foe, the majors-leading Milwaukee Brewers. It was the Reds' third straight series triumph, which began with taking two of three games against the Cubs in Chicago. On Friday, with the bases loaded in the sixth inning, Jose Trevino delivered a single that drove in JJ Bleday and Eugenio Suarez to put the Reds ahead 6-4. Suarez's hit two batters earlier allowed Elly De La Cruz to tie the game at 4-4. "Just take the moment for what it is, whether you succeed in it, great. If you fail in it, it's ok, you learn from it," said Trevino, 33. "Been in plenty of those situations my whole career. I tend to gravitate to, and like, those situations. I don't know why." --Field Level Media

item.title: Sandro Mazzola, famoso delantero del Inter y de la selección italiana, fallece a los 83 años
item.description: El exdelantero de la selección italiana Sandro Mazzola, que pasó los 17 años de su carrera profesional en el Inter de Milán, falleció a los 83 años, informó el club el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El exdelantero de la selección italiana Sandro Mazzola, que pasó los 17 años de su carrera profesional en el Inter de Milán, falleció a los 83 años, informó el club el sábado. Mazzola, considerado un emblema del Inter, marcó 158 goles en 565 partidos, lo que ayudó al equipo a ganar cuatro títulos de la Serie A y dos Copas de Europa. Formó parte de la selección italiana que ganó la Eurocopa de 1968 y llegó a la final del Mundial de México dos años después. "Sandro Mazzola fue uno de los mejores futbolistas de la historia. No solo en la historia de los Nerazzurri", dijo el Inter en un comunicado publicado en su página web oficial, en el que usó el apodo del equipo. "Él era la historia del Inter: se incorporó al club cuando era un niño y nunca lo abandonó". La primera ministra Giorgia Meloni dijo que Italia había perdido a una de las figuras más queridas de su fútbol. "Aportó alegría y pasión a generaciones de italianos, dejando una huella imborrable en nuestra nación", publicó en las redes sociales. Mazzola tenía seis años cuando su padre, Valentino —también internacional con Italia—, falleció en la catástrofe aérea de Superga, un accidente de avión ocurrido en mayo de 1949 en el que pereció toda la plantilla del Torino cuando regresaba de un partido en Lisboa. A los 18 años, Mazzola debutó con el primer equipo cuando el Inter alineó a su equipo juvenil en un partido contra la Juventus, después de que la Federación Italiana revocó una decisión que otorgaba al Inter una victoria por 2-0 tras una invasión del terreno de juego por parte de los aficionados de la Juventus y ordenó la repetición del partido. Mazzola, que de niño había sido mascota del Inter, terminó un examen escolar antes de viajar a Turín, donde marcó el único gol del Inter de penal en la derrota por 9-1 ante la Juventus. Rápidamente se convirtió en titular del primer equipo y ayudó al Inter a ganar su primera Copa de Europa en 1964, al marcar un doblete en la victoria por 3-1 sobre el Real Madrid en la final. Desempeñó un papel clave cuando el Inter volvió a ganar el título la temporada siguiente. Mazzola se retiró en 1977 y más tarde ocupó el cargo de director deportivo del Inter. También llegó a ser director deportivo del Torino, el club de su padre. "La estrella del bigote brilló sobre el terreno de juego, y sigue brillando hoy en día. Como solía decir, tenía un último deseo: ser recordado como un buen hombre, alguien que sigue luchando incluso cuando ganar es imposible, como en aquel 9-1", dijo el Inter.

item.title: Arabie saoudite-Explosions et fumée près de l'aéroport de Ryad après une alerte
item.description: Une importante colonne de fumée était visible samedi près de l'aéroport principal de Ryad après des détonations et des alertes émises pendant la nuit par l'Arabie saoudite pour signaler une potentielle menace autour de la capitale, dans un contexte d'aggravation des attaques menées par les Houthis du Yémen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une importante colonne de fumée était visible samedi près de l'aéroport principal de Ryad après des détonations et des alertes émises pendant la nuit par l'Arabie saoudite pour signaler une potentielle menace autour de la capitale, dans un contexte d'aggravation des attaques menées par les Houthis du Yémen. Une vidéo et des photos de Reuters montrent un immense panache de fumée noire s'élevant dans le secteur en question, avec au premier plan l'autoroute menant à l'aéroport, le terminal principal et d'autres installations. Dans cette vidéo, on peut voir des flammes s'élever derrière ce qui semble être des réservoirs de carburant. Le service de presse du gouvernement saoudien n'a fait aucun commentaire dans l'immédiat concernant la fumée et les alertes émises pendant la nuit. La protection civile saoudienne a envoyé ces alertes par téléphone pendant la nuit, faisant état d'un potentiel risque d'attaques aériennes à Ryad et dans la ville d'Al-Kharj, à l'est de la capitale, avant de lever l'alerte samedi dans la matinée. Un journaliste de Reuters présent dans le quartier d'Olaya, à Ryad, a entendu des détonations avant que la levée de l'alerte ne soit annoncée.

item.title: Groenlandia y Dinamarca dicen que el acuerdo con EEUU no supondrá una cesión de soberanía
item.description: Dinamarca y Groenlandia dijeron el sábado que ningún acuerdo con Estados Unidos pondría en peligro la soberanía de Groenlandia, después de que el presidente Donald Trump sostuvo que este le otorgaría a Washington "control permanente" sobre la seguridad de la isla ártica, sin que quedara claro su alcance exacto.
item.dc:creator: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen, Tom Little
item.content:encoded: Dinamarca y Groenlandia dijeron el sábado que ningún acuerdo con Estados Unidos pondría en peligro la soberanía de Groenlandia, después de que el presidente Donald Trump sostuvo que este le otorgaría a Washington "control permanente" sobre la seguridad de la isla ártica, sin que quedara claro su alcance exacto. Estados Unidos, Dinamarca y Groenlandia anunciaron a última hora del viernes que habían alcanzado un acuerdo para que Estados Unidos establezca una presencia militar significativa en Groenlandia, a la vez que se prohíbe a los adversarios de Washington construir sus propias bases en la isla. No se han hecho públicos los detalles, entre ellos el grado de presencia militar estadounidense en el territorio danés autónomo ni si se cedería a Washington algún poder formal sobre la política exterior y los recursos. Dinamarca y Groenlandia expresaron su esperanza de que el acuerdo, cuya firma está prevista durante la Asamblea General de la ONU la próxima semana, ponga fin a meses de incertidumbre provocados por las amenazas de Trump de hacerse con el control de Groenlandia. "La próxima semana podría ser una buena semana para Groenlandia, Dinamarca y Estados Unidos", dijo el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Dinamarca, Lars Lokke Rasmussen, en un comunicado publicado en Facebook el sábado. "Esperamos que este periodo de incertidumbre dé paso a un acuerdo vinculante que refuerce la seguridad en el Ártico y el Atlántico Norte y, con ello, nuestra seguridad común en el seno de la OTAN y Europa, respetando al mismo tiempo las líneas rojas del Reino (danés)", añadió. Dinamarca y Groenlandia han insistido en repetidas ocasiones en que Washington respete la soberanía del Reino de Dinamarca y acepte que Groenlandia no está en venta. LA VISIÓN DE TRUMP Trump dijo el viernes por la noche en Truth Social que, en virtud de un acuerdo, "Estados Unidos tendrá PARA SIEMPRE plena capacidad para hacer lo que sea necesario en Groenlandia con el fin de garantizar y defender la seguridad de Groenlandia y de los Estados Unidos de América". El acuerdo "otorga a Estados Unidos el control permanente sobre la seguridad y todas las demás necesidades en Groenlandia", señaló Trump, añadiendo que nunca se permitiría a ningún adversario tener una base o presencia militar en Groenlandia, ni realizar inversiones sensibles allí, sin la aprobación expresa por escrito de Washington. Trump hizo el anuncio después de que Reuters informó en exclusiva de que Estados Unidos y Dinamarca estaban a punto de cerrar un acuerdo. "Probablemente este no sea el final de las ambiciones del presidente Trump respecto a Groenlandia y, desde luego, tampoco el final del interés estratégico de Estados Unidos en el territorio y sus recursos", dijo Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, profesor de ciencias políticas de la Universidad de Copenhague. Si Copenhague cede algún poder formal a Washington, esto plantea en Groenlandia la pregunta de si "esto supone el inicio de la sustitución de la relación colonial con Dinamarca por una relación colonial con Estados Unidos", añadió. El primer ministro de Groenlandia, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, dijo el sábado que estaba satisfecho con el acuerdo propuesto: "El acuerdo reconoce la soberanía y la integridad territorial de nuestro Reino, así como el derecho del pueblo groenlandés a la autodeterminación", dijo en una publicación en Facebook. Un portavoz de la OTAN comunicó el sábado que la alianza acogía con satisfacción el acuerdo, que "contribuiría a promover la seguridad, la estabilidad y la cooperación en esta región vital".

item.title: Russia-backed South Ossetia elects leader close to Moscow
item.description: A former Russian federal official has been elected president of South Ossetia, a Russia-backed breakaway region of Georgia, in a vote Moscow hailed on Saturday as a sign of the territory's desire for closer ties with Moscow.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Papachristou
item.content:encoded: A former Russian federal official has been elected president of South Ossetia, a Russia-backed breakaway region of Georgia, in a vote Moscow hailed on Saturday as a sign of the territory's desire for closer ties with Moscow. Marat Kambolov, the new president, is from North Ossetia, a Russian republic on the other side of the Caucasus mountains from South Ossetia. He has no previous ties to South Ossetia, which broke away from Georgia during the collapse of the Soviet Union in the early 1990s and later secured de facto independence with Russian backing. A brief war between Russia and Georgia in 2008 drove Georgian forces from parts of the territory they had previously controlled. Moscow welcomed Kambolov's victory. "The results demonstrate South Ossetian society's widespread desire for domestic political stability, progress and the comprehensive development of ties with the Russian Federation," the Foreign Ministry said. South Ossetia and Russia signed a treaty in May that deepened cooperation on defence, foreign and security policy and set out plans to integrate energy grids and transport networks. Georgia condemned the treaty as an attempt by Russia to cement its "de facto annexation" of South Ossetia and Abkhazia, another Russia-backed breakaway Georgian region. Tbilisi also criticised Russia's decision to open polling stations in both territories for its [USN:L1N45B029 TEXT:"State Duma election"]s running from September 18 to 20. PUTIN SENDS CONGRATULATIONS The 61-year-old Kambolov previously held senior posts in Russian federal government bodies, including in the education ministry. He was appointed South Ossetia's prime minister in June after Alan Gagloyev stepped down as president to become an adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Putin congratulated Kambolov on Saturday in a telegram published on the Kremlin's website. In a victory speech in the South Ossetian capital Tskhinvali, Kambolov pledged to improve living standards in the region. "We have a great deal of work ahead of us. Only together can we change our republic, our Tskhinvali!" he said. South Ossetia, with a population of about 50,000, is heavily dependent on Russia for food, equipment and energy imports and has little industry of its own. Moscow funds public-sector wages, pensions and major infrastructure projects and operates a military base in the territory. Russian state media said Kambolov won 85% of the vote in Friday's election, with his rivals polling in the single digits. Turnout was 73%.

item.title: Team performance head Demko banned for 10 years for ethics code breaches
item.description: Ladislav Demko, former head of performance at the UCI Women’s Continental Hess Team, has been banned from all cycling-related activity for 10 years by the International Cycling Union's ethics commission for multiple breaches of its ethics code.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ladislav Demko, former head of performance at the UCI Women’s Continental Hess Team, has been banned from all cycling-related activity for 10 years by the International Cycling Union's ethics commission for multiple breaches of its ethics code. The Ethics Commission, a body independent from the UCI, found that Demko had "fallen short" of the standards required by the ethics code and had abused his position of power. It said an investigation had been opened following complaints from former staff members at Hess Cycling Team and from a rider who was in a consensual relationship with Demko while he was her coach, "concerning allegations of harassment and psychological abuse". Demko had subjected the rider to isolation, humiliation, intimidation and infantilisation, the commission said in a statement. Demko said the accusations stemmed from the frustrations of two staff who had been dismissed by the team. "I am not willing to ruin my savings and have decided to walk away from the world of professional cycling for good," he told Reuters on Saturday. The Slovak said that he had not yet exercised his right to file an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, but would ask for the case to be reopened in the future. He was ordered to pay a fine and the costs of the legal proceedings. The amounts were not disclosed. Hess Cycling Team was founded in 2023 but in August 2025 owner Rolf Hess, a Swiss businessman, announced on Instagram that the team had ceased operations for financial reasons.

item.title: Inside China's AI race
item.description: What does the fight to dominate AI look like from inside China?
item.content:encoded: Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app. As the US and China race to dominate artificial intelligence, Reuters correspondents Eduardo Baptista and Laurie Chen say the two countries aren't even playing the same game. On this episode of On Assignment, they take us inside China's AI industry - from Beijing's push to weave AI into every corner of society, to the murky world of chip access, distillation and export controls. Hear what it takes to report on one of the most fast-moving industries on Earth, and why the answer to "who's winning" may depend entirely on how you define the race.
